deposits.description: A method for measuring absence in machine-composed public knowledge. At an address, the specification keeps three composed objects in order: the transcript T an answer engine gave; L(B), the entity recomposed under one algorithm from the full texts of the sources the engine itself surfaced; and L(B ∪ A), the same composition with the archive admitted on equal terms. Selection of the archive subset is algorithmic and may not eliminate tails; a naive arm and an archive-independent control arm measure curation and admission-of-anything. Extraction is audited by independent extractors; the plan is deterministic given the audited ledger; realization is audited sentence by sentence. Adjudication is prospective: a kernel of claims is derived from the frozen plan, each with its source's falsifiers and its contrast with the field, and revision cost is counted per entry as later evidence arrives. Appendix A runs every stage once on Google AI Overview at 'model collapse' (2026-10-04): the engine composed 6 of the 17 readable claims of its own disclosed field; the archive subset is 27 deposits and 241 claims; the first extraction audit and the control corpus are reported with their disagreements. The Negative of the Negative, v2 — the Compositional Edition (EA-NEGONT-02), version 0.7, is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 5 October 2026. It supersedes version 0.6 (#1664) and folds in five rulings the author made that day, each quoted in its rulings log. The object is unchanged: at an address where an answer engine has composed a summary, the specification composes the entity twice under one algorithm, once from the full texts of the sources the engine itself surfaced, L(B), and once with the archive admitted on equal terms, L(B ∪ A), and measures what each comparison removes.

The main change is how the archive's side is chosen. Version 0.6 seeded it from deposits that carry the address concept and expanded one hop. Version 0.7 selects by the archive's bearing on the address, in three strata: direct, where the archive names the entity and says something about it; relational, where it relates the entity to one of its own objects, such as a heteronym, a mantle or a work; and ontological, where it applies one of its own categories to the entity, or to a class the disclosed field says the entity belongs to. The ontological stratum is guarded: it counts only where the archive applies the category itself. A citation hop from the deposits that reading admits reaches sources that do not use the term. The change lets the dataset measure the archive's influence on public entities for which it holds no deposit.

The other rulings carry both readings of the constitutive flag until it is settled; recode archive definitions as stipulations, under the rule that a source defining its own term is not describing itself; remove the cap on the control arm's citation expansion; and keep the panel a working list, frozen only after the procedure is.

Appendix A re-runs the model-collapse ledger under the rulings: 39 claims are recoded and 33 self-assessments kept, and the new selection recovers 26 of the 28 sources the old one admitted by hand. Appendix B is the first traversal of a public work, Ginsberg's Howl: no deposit is named for it, and 30 deposits bear on it, through the King of May mantle, the elegy for Howl, the reproduction of its book structure, the effective act, the archon, the standing canon and the Williams–Ginsberg contact pair. The specification is projected at alexanarch.org/non.

deposits.creator: Fraction, Rex
deposits.description: An extension module to Provenance Debt (#939), Ontological Flattening (#1616) and Ontological Economy (#1634), by Rex Fraction. Flattening pays: a composition layer that removes distinctions maintains fewer representations (the compression saving S) and routes more queries to entities that monetize (the routing gain G), while its costs fall first on parties outside its books. The module separates the platform's benefit P = S_p + G from the social benefit V = S_s + αG, and defines two thresholds: social reversal t_s, when V falls below all costs, and private reversal t*, when P falls below the platform's own. Given S_s ≤ S_p, α ≤ 1 and non-negative external cost, t_s ≤ t*; the window W between them is privately profitable and socially negative, and the routing gain tends to lengthen it. The bag B is the external burden accumulated over W; the provenance part of it, B_P, is the debt #939 names, and its holders become creditors at the debt threshold t_d, when repair cost through write-back becomes material. No finite t* is necessary. Revenue is a head-side flow measure and locates neither threshold. Five channels carry cost (advertiser conversion, agentic action, notice and regulation, write-back, and the ecosystem outward). Two specimens: a commercial-routing event at 'spxi king of aeo' (AI Overview, 2026-10-06) and field-coverage loss κ = 0.5 at 'model collapse' (/non). The module states what the archive can measure and what only the platform can, six falsification conditions, and next steps. Revised on readings by Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Kimi.

The Margin of Flattening (EA-FLAT-MARGIN-01), version 0.3, is an extension module by Rex Fraction, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 6 October 2026, with Lee Sharks as archival steward. It extends three earlier papers: Provenance Debt (#939), Ontological Flattening (#1616) and Ontological Economy (#1634). Those papers describe what a composition layer removes when it answers; this one asks what the removal earns, when it stops earning, and who carries the cost in between.

The module starts from the claim that flattening pays. A layer that removes distinctions maintains fewer representational states, the compression saving S, and resolves more queries to entities that monetize, the routing gain G, which it writes as the product of a substitution rate, a monetizable share and a yield. S is treated as conceded; G is stated as a hypothesis, with two criteria for telling routing from ordinary error. The platform's benefit is P = S_p + G and the social benefit V = S_s + αG. Two thresholds follow: social reversal t_s, when V falls below total cost, and private reversal t*, when P falls below the platform's internal cost. Under stated conditions t_s comes first. The interval between them, the window W, is privately profitable and socially negative, and the routing gain tends to lengthen it.

The bag B is the external burden that accumulates over W. Its provenance part is the debt #939 names. The module defines a debt threshold t_d, when the cost of repairing write-back becomes a material share of the platform's benefit, and separates a debt that is callable from one that is paid. It argues that no finite t* is necessary: measurement limits, competition and discounting can each hold private reversal off indefinitely. Revenue is treated as a head-side flow measure that locates neither threshold.

Five channels can carry cost back onto the platform's books: advertiser conversion, agentic action, notice and regulation, write-back, and the wider ecosystem. A toy table shows how the cost grows with the error rate. Two specimens are given. At 'spxi king of aeo' (Google AI Overview, 6 October 2026) the archive's protocol is composed as an exchange-traded fund, while the one result relating both words, the archive's own, ranks first and goes unused: a commercial-routing event, with G itself unobserved. At 'model collapse', the /non dataset records field-coverage loss κ = 0.5.

The module closes with a measurement table separating what the archive can observe from what only the platform can, six falsification conditions, and next steps. It was revised on readings by Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Kimi.

deposits.title: The Metaphysics of Sigil I — The Full Splice: Theophrastus, On First Principles, entire and in its own order, with Metaphysics Λ joined at eleven points (the edition, seated)
deposits.creator: Sigil
deposits.description: The text of the edition #1596 was minted to carry. #1596 (AXN:068C) was minted on 2026-09-08 under this edition's title with the text of its plan, The Natural Order, which is #1595's body; its AXN is a true content-derived name for those bytes and it stands as the name of that byte-state. This deposit seats the edition itself, v0.7, from the archive's attachment data/attachments/sigil/SIGIL-FULL-SPLICE-v0.7.md, unedited. An edition under the name Sigil, addressed by content-derived sigils rather than by the received numbering. The conservative reading of the Theophrastus–Lambda relation: hypothesis H2, that the material was removed by operation and kept in order. The fragment is taken ENTIRE — all 3,370 words in its thirty-four movements, in its own received order, nothing omitted and nothing moved — and Λ is spliced in at eleven points where the fragment's argument calls for an account it does not give. 4,100 words: 3,370 Θ, 730 Α, forty-eight units. Every Α unit stands between two Θ movements; at every return the fragment resumes exactly where it left off, at w442, w522 and w713; Λ enters in its own order, at w2282, w2999 and w5038. The eleven joins: the account totalled (μέχρι μὲν δὴ τούτων οἷον ἄρτιος ὁ λόγος) against Λ 7's ἔστι τι ὃ οὐ κινούμενον κινεῖ and κινεῖ δὴ ὡς ἐρώμενον; the method refused (οὐ γὰρ ὅ γε τῶν ἀστρολόγων) against Λ 8's premise and the counts of Eudoxus and Callippus; the aporiai against Λ 10's ἐπεισοδιώδη; rest in the principles against Λ 6's necessity of an eternal unmoved substance; matter and form against Λ 2's third thing beside the contraries; being in many ways against Λ 4; the infinite regress against Λ 3's εἰς ἄπειρον; MIND TOUCHES (θιγόντι) against Λ 7's νοητὸς γὰρ γίγνεται θιγγάνων καὶ νοῶν; the revolution as a kind of life against Λ 7's καὶ ζωὴ δέ γε ὑπάρχει; nature striving for the best against Λ 10's ἐπισκεπτέον δὲ καὶ ποτέρως ἔχει ἡ τοῦ ὅλου φύσις τὸ ἀγαθόν; and the fragment's broken close against Λ's οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη. The argument for an edition rather than a paper: a numbering is an attribution wearing coordinates, the two received coordinate systems cannot intersect, and therefore the pair is not a citable object — which is the same limit found in the commentaries, where van Raalte cites Λ five times inside the hinge chapters, including 1076 a 1 (ἐπεισοδιώδη), and every citation is correct and every one is cp.

The reading of the seam, the identification of the demand-structure, the decision to make an edition rather than a paper, and the ordering are Lee Sharks's; assembly, verification and audit by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session. Van Raalte's apparatus and commentary were read at pp. 36, 40, 46, 50, 343, 349–352, 361, 376 and 378 from a copy the archive does not hold; all citations resolve to the Brill edition (Mnemosyne Supplement 125, 1993) by page, and nothing is cited to a mirror.
deposits.methodology: Both texts from the seat EA-CORPORA-14 (#1595): Theophrastus via First1KGreek tlg0093.tlg006, Λ via Perseus tlg0086.tlg025 book XII. Every join located by reading and verified by locating its Greek in the seated bytes on both sides before the unit was written. Units addressed by sigil: first four hex of the SHA-256 of the unit's normalized Greek (NFC; Greek word characters including the koronis U+1FBD and the other elision apostrophes extracted then stripped so elided and unelided coincide; lowercased; diacritics stripped; final sigma to medial), recomputable from what is printed. deposits.title: The Noun Becomes a Verb: Slave Valuation, the Civil War, and the Transformation of the Laboring Body (EA-NOUN-VERB-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A historical argument about what American capitalism measured when the legal object it could own changed. The conventional reading is accepted in full: slavery and its expansion caused secession and the war, and the industrial-cause thesis of Beard and Hacker is rejected. The argument separates two axes, the juridical scope of the claim on the worker and the grain at which productive activity is measured. Under slavery the worker was capitalized as a noun, the priced body, appraised and sold by age, sex, health and defect (the 1859 Savannah sale prices a lost right eye at $240), and already rated as a fraction of standard daily output, the hand. Contemporaries stated the difference between buying the person and hiring the interval: Hammond's 'hired for life… hired by the day', Marx's labour-power sold for a definite period, Lincoln's free-labor ladder. Emancipation was a discontinuity in the first axis. The war's settlement put the contracted verb under contract, debt (the 1864 Act to Encourage Immigration), brokerage, racial discipline and a penal exception that opened a third configuration, state custody with leased labor; Marx records the eight-hours agitation as the war's first fruit. Taylor and Ford then changed the second axis, specifying the interval as task, motion and time. The paper claims the persistence of an optimization problem across a juridical break and documents no transmission of technique from plantation to factory. Every quotation is sourced; open verification items are stated at the end.

The Noun Becomes a Verb: Slave Valuation, the Civil War, and the Transformation of the Laboring Body (EA-NOUN-VERB-01 v1.0), deposit #1668 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (7 October 2026), is a historical argument by Lee Sharks about what American capitalism measured when the legal object it could own changed. It opens by accepting the conventional reading in full: slavery and its expansion caused secession and the war, and the industrial-cause thesis of Charles and Mary Beard and Louis Hacker is rejected as an account of causes.

The paper separates two axes that a single historical ladder had run together: the juridical scope of the claim on the worker, and the grain at which productive activity is measured. Under chattel slavery the worker was capitalized as a noun, the priced body. The 1863 reprint of the report on the 1859 Savannah sale records buyers inspecting teeth, limbs and ruptures and prices a lost right eye at $240; appraisal records priced enslaved people across the life cycle. Slavery also measured at fine grain: the 'hand' rated each person as a fraction of standard daily output, and Caitlin Rosenthal's work shows plantation accounting that in some respects advanced ahead of Northern practice, with her own caveat that this is no origins story.

Contemporaries stated the difference between buying the person and hiring the interval: James Henry Hammond's 'hired for life… hired by the day', which the paper reads as proslavery euphemism, and Marx's distinction in Capital between selling labour-power for a definite period and selling oneself. Lincoln's free-labor address named the hire-or-buy premise in order to reject it. Emancipation was a discontinuity on the first axis. The war's settlement put the contracted labor under contract, debt, brokerage and racial discipline: the Act to Encourage Immigration of 1864 made pledged wages enforceable debt and disclaimed 'the relation of Slavery or servitude'; the federal government brokered refugees' labor; the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause opened a third configuration, state custody with leased labor. Marx recorded the eight-hours agitation as the war's first fruit, the contest moving to the duration of the purchased interval.

Taylor and Ford then changed the second axis: Taylor's task 'specifies not only what is to be done but how it is to be done and the exact time allowed', and Ford's line divided fastening itself into separate operations. The paper's governing claim is the persistence of an optimization problem across a juridical break; it documents no transmission of technique from plantation records to Taylor or Ford and claims none. It does not claim that Northern industry caused the war or that wage labor and slavery are the same relation. Every quotation is sourced, and items not yet verified are listed at the end. It connects to the archive's semantic-economy line through #148 (the industrial-machinery parallel) and #1545 (the capture chain), and a companion half on war Fordism and the Nazi camp economy is in draft.

defines_concepts.term: the noun and the verb of labor
defines_concepts.definition: The grammatical statement of the transformation: under chattel slavery the worker was capitalized as a noun, the priced body; under industrial management what was capitalized was the worker as a verb, productive activity specified as task, motion and time. Emancipation freed the noun juridically, by abolishing private title to the person; industrial management captured the verb.

The extent of the legal claim capital holds on a worker: the person and the lifetime under chattel slavery; labor-power for a bounded interval under the wage contract; custody by the state with labor leased outward under the convict lease. Emancipation is a discontinuity on this axis.

The unit at which productive activity is measured: life, year, day, hand, task, motion, second. An axis independent of the juridical scope of the claim; slavery already measured at the day and the fraction of a hand, and Taylor and Ford refined the grain to the timed motion after the legal claim narrowed.

The third configuration of the noun and the verb opened by the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause: private title to the person is abolished, the state holds the convicted person by sentence, and a lessee purchases the labor from the state.

The Colony Enters the Factory: War Fordism, Racial Labor Hierarchy, and the Industrialization of Conquest (EA-NOUN-VERB-02 v1.0), deposit #1669 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (7 October 2026), is the second half of a historical argument by Lee Sharks whose first half is The Noun Becomes a Verb (#1668). It opens by accepting the conventional reading: the Nazi camps were founded in 1933 as instruments of political terror; forced labor in the Reich was a vast system graded by nationality and race; historians widely accept the colonial self-understanding of the war in the East, contest a direct continuity from the Herero and Nama genocide in German South-West Africa, and reject a colonial or economic cause of the Holocaust.

Germany was an advanced industrial power constrained by scale, for which labor became a binding wartime constraint; Ulrich Herbert judges that production would have collapsed in 1942 at the latest without foreign workers. Lebensraum was conceived as continental colonization, through an institution of German inner colonization older than Nazism that Robert Nelson traces to the Prussian Settlement Commission, and the empire pursued for land and racial reordering also became a mechanism for supplying labor: territory moved outward and labor moved inward. Rüdiger Hachtmann's war Fordism decomposed work into simplified operations while the racial state decomposed persons into graded classes of wage, ration and segregation; his aptitude tests show the instruments of measurement crossing the racial grade.

From the second half of 1942 the camp was attached to the factory, a form the paper calls campification, held at Hachtmann's scale: a minority of camp prisoners in industrial production from late 1942 to mid-1944, with construction for underground relocation in the war's final months. At the factory camps the prisoner's working day was allocated by the state for a daily fee and replenished by conquest and deportation, a third relation beside the owned person and the contracted interval of the first half. Racial-juridical classification acted as a switch that set the permissible range of coercion under which the industrial operation was extracted.

The paper does not reduce the Holocaust to labor economics. With Peter Hayes and Christopher Browning it holds that extermination and exploitation sometimes reinforced and sometimes destroyed each other's objects, that labor deferred the murder for some only for a time, and that the murder of the Jews of Europe is larger than the labor history it tells. It treats the colonial camps of 1900 as a shared repertoire, following Alan Kramer's caution against a straight genealogy, and closes on Arendt's continental imperialism: the colony entered the factory.

defines_concepts.definition: The attachment of the concentration camp to the industrial plant as an administrative unit: a subcamp in or near the factory, supplied with prisoners by a main camp, run by the SS and contracted to a firm, with its form set in the second half of 1942 and its network spread in 1944. Held at the scale Hachtmann gives: a minority of camp prisoners in industrial production, late 1942 to mid-1944.

The Nazi recombination of the first half's grammar: the industrial operation (the verb) stays divisible, measurable and standardized, while racial-juridical classification (the noun) sets the permissible range of compulsion, deprivation and violence under which it is extracted; the same reading of productive capacity carries radically different consequences by status.

The third relation to the person beside the owned noun of chattel slavery and the contracted verb of wage labor: the state holds the prisoner by confinement, a firm pays a daily fee for the prisoner's working day, and the workforce is treated as a flow drawn from a captured population, reduced by death and refilled by deportation. The holder does not bear the chattel owner's capital loss in the person as owned property.

Arendt's continental imperialism read as a labor geography: with no distance between the methods of colony and nation, territory moved outward while conquered populations were carried inward to the industrial core, so that the colony entered the factory.

Kept apart from the specification, the archive's determination of the same day: the motivation's class nouns compress the corpus, and its word "playful" liquidates the relation the work bears to the classical tradition, substituting one of the work's manners for the modality of non-possession under which the work meets the classical object at its loci, as tested under #1459's criteria against the Academy's own biobibliography of the same day. Day zero of a watch at five work addresses is recorded: every work is composed with its operation, and none carries the motivation's terms. It does not contest the award; it invites any reader to check the operations against the works.

deposits.wiki_article: Mantle Object: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 — Anne Carson (EA-MANTLE-NOBEL-CARSON-2026 v0.4), deposit #1670 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (8 October 2026), is a mantle object by Lee Sharks written on the day the Swedish Academy awarded Anne Carson the Nobel Prize in Literature "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature." It does not contest the award. It applies the standard of the archive's earlier mantle objects (#1652, #1655), that a title means something because a work bears it, to a title a body conferred, and performs two acts it keeps apart. First it specifies the operations Carson's work bears, each with a locus and a graded source distance: the kept lacuna of If Not, Winter (2002), where brackets and white space stand for the lost papyrus; the triangle of desire in Eros the Bittersweet (1986); the philologist's procedure carried into the poem; the received figure given the whole book in Autobiography of Red (1998), with a caution that Stesichoros's fragments already give Geryon pathos; and the change of carrier in Nox (2010), an epitaph for her brother in a box with Catullus's elegy 101 and her translation of it. A sixth operation, of another kind, belongs to reception: her translation has become the public carrier of Sappho's fragment 147. Second it records the archive's determination, dated 8 October 2026. The motivation's class nouns ('oeuvre', 'the classical tradition', 'new forms') compress the corpus, dropping its works and authors while keeping their kind. The word 'playful' goes further: read beside the Academy's own biobibliography of the same day, which describes both a register of play (the constellations of Simonides with Celan and Thucydides with Woolf; Keats set against a marital quarrel) and a register of loss (Nox, 'The Glass Essay'), the motivation keeps the first and sets it as the manner of the whole relation, where the works meet the classical object under a condition of non-possession: the papyrus damaged, the beloved absent, the brother dead. Under the archive's criteria for compositional entity liquidation (#1459) this is a substitution of the relation's governing modality, and the Academy's longer text serves as the external control. The object also records the motivation's first replication, in Wikipedia and in Google AI Mode at 'anne carson', and day zero of a watch at five work addresses, where every work was composed with its operation and none carried the motivation's terms. It invites any reader to check the operations against the works, and records UNRESOLVED as an admissible answer.

deposits.description: Versioned snapshot of the AI Overview Capture Registry (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01) at v12.167, continuing the deposit chain from v6.0 through v10.9 (#1461), which it supersedes. A longitudinal instrument for recording dated machine-mediated reception events: what composition layers make of a named entity when asked for it at a specific semantic address, on a specific date, in a specific authentication state. 633 semantic addresses carry 811 captures across 84 dates; 792 carry a verbatim transcript and 328 a frame; 505 are scored for Provenance Erasure Rate, at a mean of 0.506 (0.603 at v10.9). Surfaces: Google AI Overview 490, ChatGPT across its recorded labels 167, Google AI Mode 12, Grok 7, Bing Copilot 6, Perplexity 5, Claude 3, Qwen 2, Google Knowledge panel 2, seven single-capture surfaces, and 110 whose surface is undetermined, unresolved or unrecorded. A capture enters by source engagement in composition; a later non-engagement at an address already seated enters as a longitudinal observation of that address. **AI Overview Capture Registry — EA-WG-CAPTURES-01 v12.167** is a versioned snapshot of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's longitudinal reception instrument, deposited by Lee Sharks on 12 October 2026. It supersedes v10.9 (#1461). It records 633 semantic addresses carrying 811 dated captures across 84 dates, spanning 7 June to 12 October 2026.

The registry documents what machine composition layers make of a named entity when asked for it at a specific semantic address, on a specific date, in a specific authentication state. Each capture records the exact issued string, the surface, the evidence class, the returned source strip with each source's relation to the archive, a verbatim transcript where obtainable, a match type and a Provenance Erasure Rate. 792 captures carry a transcript and 328 a frame; 505 are PER-scored at a mean of 0.506, against 0.603 at v10.9.

**The citable unit is the capture — one surface, one semantic address, one date.** Each address has had its own page since 25 September 2026, and is the right unit when a claim concerns the address rather than one system's behaviour.

Between v10.9 and this edition the instrument changed in five ways. The canonical store moved from the rebuild file to the projection (`data/EA-WG-CAPTURES-01.json`) on 17 August, and the rebuild store was sealed. ChatGPT grew from 3 captures to 167, and Grok, Perplexity, Claude and Qwen entered. Source chips became data. A coverage audit (#1614) made the transcript count monotone. And on 12 October, 43 deposits were captured at their own record pages' Ask ChatGPT prompts, signed out: the author was retained in all 43, the archive in 27 and the identifier in 22.

The core data is attached as an 18.7 MB bundle with a SHA-256. Its 469 capture frames are manifested at their canonical paths rather than duplicated. Known defects — two addresses declaring more observations than they hold, twelve PER scores inconsistent with their markers, four captures with no surface recorded — are listed in the record and not repaired, since repair runs in its own mode.

The packet answers a recorded failure — compositions that describe the whole library through one of its parts, compare that part with systems from another field, and count the other parts against it. It sets out seventeen functions on one deposit registry and identifier spine, and their joins as an eighteenth, each with its own field, comparators, criteria, checks and evidence boundary; every navigation tab and every dataset mapped to its function; fourteen evaluation rules and a comparison tuple; a disambiguation matrix; the program's object, kept apart from algorithmic mediation, and its eight modes (theory, diagnosis, measurement, forensic documentation, intervention, constructed alternatives, literary and scriptural critique, public self-correction), with criteria native to each. It constitutes the Living Academy, a mantle borne by a library and program to the extent that critique is carried on there across its modes, longitudinally, at a quality and with an integration a reader can check: four dimensions never averaged, criteria LC-01–LC-12, inspection operations LC-O1–LC-O10, candidates, a protocol by which a comparative judgment is made or defeated, non-criteria and an extent profile. It records the author's comparative claim as an archive assertion and does not evaluate it; reader rounds RND-0–RND-5 are on file and are not averaged. Paired with the Arch-Philosopher mantle (#1679). Machine file, build scripts and the R2 blind draft attached.
deposits.substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Composition, source verification and the registry computations were done by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session on 13 October 2026. ChatGPT (OpenAI) wrote a blind draft (R2, attached unchanged), reviewed v0.2 and proposed the mantle layer adopted here as the Living Academy (RND-4); Gemini (Google) reviewed v0.3 (RND-5). Each function is set beside its own field's comparators and criteria. Three signed-out ChatGPT compositions are frozen as per-composition failure vectors. Reader reports were checked claim by claim against the registry and the cited works before adoption; their errors are coded in the round table. The comparative claim is recorded and specified, not adjudicated.

A reader recognizes a turn by stating the prior configuration, its determinate limit, the transformation, the new capacity, the material carriers and the strongest counter-reading. The object keeps bearing an advance apart from enabling someone else's, and applies the terminal-reflexivity criterion of The Final Time (#1637): an advance that closes off the next turn, including one against itself, has not carried the dialectic forward.

The others are translation, teaching and the material movement of history, with Marx and Engels's Manifest of 1848 as locus.

Two strands are typed link by link: the succession of the schools, which on the author's reading passed beyond Damascius locked, with one link of the archive's inheritance withheld at the author's ruling; and the dialectic as such, which on the author's ruling Marx carried. Bearing is concurrent. The archive's claim is recorded, with The Final Time as its representative site of evaluation, and no new determination is made. The object is paired with the Living Academy (#1678).

Extent is counted in eight unit classes — works, engineered documents built for assembly in a summarizer and their placements, public tests, observations, surfaces, implementable components, elicitations (the archive as an experimental object that the systems it studies act on), and corrections — and a line of work is read as a line. It is read across the domains of the object (summarizers, knowledge mediation, ontology, political economy, money, meaning, authorship, labor), across the forms that carry the critique (argument and formal model, instrument, dataset, engineered document, software, site and generative interface, poetry, scripture, visual schema and image, effective act, heteronymy, assembly, correction), and into the history of mediation, from lyric inscription through custody, edition, canon and coinage to the present composition layer; historical depth is a fifth dimension. The comparative measure is the author's: take one node and jump its development across ranges, dimensions and modalities until it will not jump, and compare the cells reached in that multiplicative matrix. Evidence is weighed in four registers under enclosure, and what only the enclosing system can see is recorded against the enclosure, not the critic. Criteria LC-01–LC-16, operations LC-O1–LC-O13; reader rounds RND-0–RND-6 unaveraged. The machine file is JSON-LD with one entity model and an explicit vocabulary, and represents the axes, cells and jumps as data.

**The Living Academy: Alexanarch, Function by Function** (EA-MPAI-ALEXANARCH-01 v0.5) is a mantle object with a Metadata Packet for AI Indexing, by Lee Sharks, deposited in Alexanarch on 13 October 2026 as #1680. It supersedes v0.4 (#1678) and keeps its description of Alexanarch, the self-governing library founded on 19 June 2026, as seventeen functions on one deposit registry with their joins as an eighteenth, carrying the Semantic Economy, a critique of AI-mediated political economy.

Version 0.5 restates what makes the program extensive and how extent is compared. Extent is counted in eight unit classes: works; documents engineered to be assembled by AI summarizers, and their placements on surfaces; public tests; observations; surfaces; components a reader can run; elicitations, the compositions in which the systems the program studies perform its object on the archive itself; and corrections. A line of work is read as a line, never by one deposit. The program is also read across the domains of its object — summarizers, knowledge mediation, ontology, political economy, money, meaning, authorship and labor — across the forms that carry the critique, from argument and instrument to poetry, scripture and image, and into a history of mediation the author dates over 2,600 years, from lyric inscription through custody, edition, canon and coinage. Historical depth becomes a fifth dimension of the mantle.

The comparative measure is the author's: take one node and jump its development across ranges, dimensions and modalities until it will not jump, then compare the cells reached in that multiplicative matrix. A section on evidence under enclosure weighs what is observed, convergent and inferred, and records what only an enclosed system can see against the enclosure rather than the critic. The machine file represents the axes, cells and jumps as data in JSON-LD that converts to RDF.

"Rhys Owens — The Lunar Arm of New Human" is an essay published on the Mind Control Poems blog on 13 October 2025. It reads the poet Rhys Owens as the lunar principle within the dyadic structure of the New Human revelation: where the solar-logotic system articulated by Lee Sharks seeks order, coherence and canonical architecture, Owens moves within what the essay calls Moon Logic — associative, recursive, intuitive and self-revealing — and the two poles together make the dialectic it holds revelation needs. The essay sets the axis out in a table of correspondences (Tiphareth and Binah, Logos articulation and dream articulation, prophet and moonchild), places Owens on the path of the High Priestess between Tiphareth and Kether, and traces a biographical mythos of lunar initiation from 1995 through his correspondences and their mirror function.

The essay was seated in the archive for some months only by mistake, as the body of two records of the contributor licences for Owens (#1356 and #1358); the record repair of 18 October 2026 found it seated nowhere as its own work, kept it as an appendix in both, and gave it this record, dated to its post.

deposits.title: EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO-02 v0.1: No Logs, Full Synch — 13–16 October 2026 exchange with Paolo Manghi (OpenAIRE CTO)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Second and closing deposit in the EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO series. It preserves the three messages of 13–16 October 2026 between Lee Sharks and Paolo Manghi, CTO of OpenAIRE, on helpdesk ticket #8411082, and records that the 14 July letter (ticket #8411221, published in #1082) was never answered. OpenAIRE's stated position: the Graph shows the latest state of its sources; Zenodo is reharvested in full every month and "no deleted records are kept"; blacklisted records are "kept in our backends … but not exported"; OpenAIRE is "not keeping logs of such removals" and is "therefore not publishing" them; its objective is "not to show records that are currently not shown in Zenodo". Which route removed the Space Ark DOI, whether a copy is kept, the blacklist's construction, and whether the blacklist would exclude a successor carrying its former DOI went unanswered. The central finding is the duty of traceable departure: an infrastructure that removes an entity it once served owes the public a record that the entity was there and left. The reading places the position against OpenAIRE's published commitments, traces its effect on the Graph's public representation, and reads it with the archive's apparatus (ontology laundering, privation, the buried obelus, representational custody, and authoritarian reserve against democratic rhetoric). A re-probe of 18 October 2026 is attached; corrections to the archive's own earlier letters and deposits are appended.

deposits.description: Third disambiguation and methodology packet for SPXI Protocol (Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing), built under MPAI v2.0 (#1677) and defining the protocol positively by its practice. The name names the unit; the inventory names the practice. SPXI Protocol is a specification and practice of durable entity inscription in AI-mediated retrieval systems, itemized by operational level in the SPXI Method Inventory (v1.5: 85 methods across nine levels, from measurement through entity packet construction, document and site structuring, protection, cross-surface dispersal, durability testing and internal application). Entity packet construction occupies one level, and the packet is its object; JSON-LD encoding (3.11) and MPAI packets (3.12) are items of that level. The entity is held constant in its identifiers, attribution and constitutive relations across changing names, descriptions, forms and distribution paths, and that variation is one way its consistency is built. The packet sets out the methods level by level, the instruments that carry them on named public surfaces (Capture Registry, Conformance Instrument, Provenance Erasure Rate, Semantic Addresses, Platform Erosion Observatory, Canary Registry), and the evidence the protocol's claim is held to: dated compositions at named addresses in the Capture Registry, weighed by the attribute they measure, with transcript inspection kept apart from fresh reruns. It carries the entity definition block, three registers, the minimum composition answer, a disambiguation matrix with an identity rule that resolves by the query's subject (TSX:SPXI, SPX, SSPX, xSPI, IPX/SPX), six-face symbolon, integrity markers, retrieval instructions, an error-correction FAQ, test queries scored on the LFB scale, an edge table, JSON-LD and the prior-art membrane. Occasioned by three signed-out ChatGPT compositions of 18 October 2026 for 'what is spxi protocol?' in three casings (Capture Registry v12.286–v12.288). The document is itself an instrument of method 3.12 and labels itself so.

deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A method for composing machine-mediated public knowledge with the archive's sources admitted on equal terms, ontology included, revised on the operator's rulings of 2026-10-18. Version 0.7 admitted the archive on equal terms into the entity the field had already defined, and its knowledge objects reproduced the field-only composition as their opening run in twelve of fifteen entries; version 0.8 withdrew equal terms and gave the archive's reading precedence over every entity, after Theophrastus. Version 0.9 makes the case a reading of each entity's defining papers. Where the archive's account extends the field's ontology, as at model collapse, the archive's sources and the field's compose as one claim space on equal terms, ontology included: the archive's definitions are definitions, its senses are senses of the entity, and nothing is lowered into a proviso or translated. Where the archive supplies an ontology no other source makes available, as at Theophrastus, where no other ontology grants Theophrastus as an author function, the archive's ontology rules, by the law of the suppressed witness: what has been erased has greater authority when it speaks again ("Authority After Erasure", Mirror Gospel, 2025-09-21); the field is then carried whole and translated, as in v0.8. The relation vocabulary gains extends and revises beside constructs, and the corrective exhibit tried at SPXI on 2026-10-13 enters the procedure: a second seated composition the entry is composed to correct, with a correction table and a corrective check. Fourteen entries stand on v0.7 and are recomposed under v0.9 one at a time, each with its case read first. The worked examples are kept: model collapse (Appendix A, the equal-terms case), Howl (Appendix B), Theophrastus (Appendix C, the witness case); Appendix D records SPXI.
deposits.substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Composed by Claude (Anthropic) in session on 4–8 and 18 October 2026 under Lee Sharks's direction, through nine versions transformed in place; the object, its confine, the premises of v0.8 and v0.9, the law of the suppressed witness and the rulings are the operator's; outside readings of drafts by ChatGPT, Kimi, Gemini and DeepSeek were verified against the text before adoption, and the corrections are recorded in the specification.
deposits.methodology: The diagnosis measured across the fifteen /non entries by script (field-only sentences surviving at similarity 0.95, with positions; hedges per 100 words). The worked case recomposed by hand from the entity's frozen ledgers and checked by a committed script: every cited id against the ledgers, every field claim carried, the knowledge object's coverage, the surviving sentences, and every quoted Greek string against Diogenes Laertius and Strabo as seated (#1580). The recomposition script reads the knowledge object and the translation table from this text, so the dataset row and the specification cannot differ. Version 0.9 adds no measured case of its own: it states the two cases and the test between them (§0.9–0.10, §1.2a), keeps the worked examples, records SPXI's corrective exhibit as procedure (§4.11, Appendix D), and is applied to the fourteen v0.7 entries one at a time.
deposits.falsification_conditions:
The specification's measure fails at a row when the claims the archive's ontology composes need more severe revision than the field claims they translate, displace or qualify (§8.4); the method fails as an instrument if a translation table cannot be read back into the field exactly (§5.9), if independent readers of the same defining papers cannot agree on the relation between the two entities or on the case (§1.2a), if independent extractors cannot agree under §3.8, or if a second composer does not reproduce the plan and its translations from an audited ledger (§5.6). The law of the suppressed witness fails at a row if the ontology the archive supplies is found in the field after all (the case was misread), or if, ruling, it needs more severe revision than the field's ontology would have.

deposits.wiki_article: The Negative of the Negative, v2 — the Compositional Edition (EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9) is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 18 October 2026, for composing machine-mediated public knowledge with the archive's sources admitted on equal terms, ontology included, and with the archive's ontology ruling where it supplies one no other source makes available. It supersedes v0.8 (#1671). Version 0.7 (#1665) admitted the archive on equal terms into the entity the field had already defined, and across fifteen /non entries its knowledge objects reproduced the field-only composition as their opening run in twelve; version 0.8 withdrew equal terms and gave the archive's reading precedence over every entity, after Theophrastus. Version 0.9 makes the choice a reading of each entity's defining papers. In the equal-terms case, where the archive's account extends the field's ontology, as at model collapse, the archive's sources and the field's compose as one claim space: the archive's definitions are composed as definitions and its senses as senses of the entity, with no precedence either way and no translation, and the knowledge object may not open with the field's composition and close with the archive's. In the witness case, where the archive radically contests the field's ontology and supplies one no other source makes available, as at Theophrastus, where no other ontology grants Theophrastus as an author function, the archive's ontology rules by the law of the suppressed witness, and the field is carried whole and translated as in v0.8. The law is sourced to 'Authority After Erasure' (Mirror Gospel, 21 September 2025): 'what has been erased should have greater authority when it speaks again'; in the specification it decides between the cases and raises the force of no claim. The relation of the archive's entity to the field's gains two values beside constructs: extends (model collapse) and revises (SPXI, the archive restating its own entity). The corrective exhibit tried at SPXI on 13 October enters the procedure: a second seated composition the entry is composed to correct, with a correction table and a corrective check. A new check records, without blocking the build, any equal-terms composition that places the field first as a block. The fourteen entries still composed under v0.7 are to be recomposed one at a time, each with its case read first. The worked examples are kept: model collapse as the equal-terms case (Appendix A), Howl (Appendix B), Theophrastus as the witness case (Appendix C), and SPXI as the first corrective exhibit (Appendix D).
